activity.label: Research note
activity.detail:
Perseverance rover:
- Landing date in UTC: February 18, 2021, 20:55 UTC
- Landing crater: Jezero Crater

Curiosity rover:
- Landing date in UTC: August 6, 2012, 05:17:57 UTC
- Landing crater: Gale Crater (specifically Aeolis Palus within Gale Crater)

Curiosity landed first, as its landing date (August 6, 2012) precedes Perseverance's landing date (February 18, 2021).

message.content: The Mars rover *Curiosity* landed on August 6, 2012, at 05:17:57 UTC in Gale crater, Mars [1]. The Mars rover *Perseverance* landed on February 18, 2021, at 20:55 UTC in Jezero crater, Mars [2]. *Curiosity* landed first.

passages.heading: *Curiosity* (rover)
passages.text:
***Curiosity*** is a Mars rover that is exploring Gale crater and Mount Sharp on Mars as part of NASA's Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) mission.<sup>[2]</sup> Launched in 2011 and landed the following year, the car-sized rover continues to operate more than a decade after its original two-year mission.

*Curiosity* was launched from Cape Canaveral, Florida, on November 26, 2011, at 15:02:00 UTC and landed on Aeolis Palus inside Gale crater on Mars on August 6, 2012, 05:17:57 UTC.<sup>[3]</sup><sup>[4]</sup><sup>[5]</sup> The Bradbury Landing site was less than 2.4 km (1.5 mi) from the center of the rover's touchdown target after a 560 million km (350 million mi) journey.<sup>[6]</sup><sup>[7]</sup>

passages.heading: *Curiosity* (rover)
passages.text: The NASA/JPL Mars Science Laboratory/*Curiosity* Project Team was awarded the 2012 Robert J. Collier Trophy by the National Aeronautic Association "In recognition of the extraordinary achievements of successfully landing *Curiosity* on Mars, advancing the nation's technological and engineering capabilities, and significantly improving humanity's understanding of ancient Martian habitable environments."<sup>[14]</sup> *Curiosity*'s rover design served as the basis for NASA's 2021 *Perseverance* mission, which carries different scientific instruments.

passages.heading: *Perseverance* (rover)
passages.text:
**Perseverance**<sup>[2]</sup> is a NASA rover that has been exploring Mars since February 18, 2021,<sup>[3]</sup><sup>[4]</sup> as part of the Mars 2020 mission. Built and managed by the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, the car-sized rover was launched on July 30, 2020,<sup>[5]</sup> from Cape Canaveral aboard an Atlas V rocket and landed in Jezero Crater, a site chosen for its ancient river delta that may preserve evidence of past microbial life.

The rover's main goals are to search for signs of ancient life, study the planet's geology and climate, and collect rock and regolith samples for possible return to Earth by a future mission. *Perseverance* also tests technologies intended to support later human exploration, including an experiment that successfully produced oxygen from the thin carbon-dioxide atmosphere.<sup>[6]</sup>

passages.heading: *Perseverance* (rover)
passages.text: Powered by a radioisotope thermoelectric generator, *Perseverance* has an expected mission duration of over a decade.<sup>[11]</sup> It has provided high-resolution panoramas, drilled and cached samples for later retrieval, and identified rocks which may have been habitable for ancient microbial life in Jezero Crater. In July 2024, it discovered the Cheyava Falls rock containing "possible biosignature." As of 6 October 2026, *Perseverance* has been active on Mars for 2001 sols (2056 total days; *5 years, 230 days*) since its landing.

Section: *Curiosity* (rover)
***Curiosity*** is a Mars rover that is exploring Gale crater and Mount Sharp on Mars as part of NASA's Mars Science Laboratory (MSL) mission.<sup>[2]</sup> Launched in 2011 and landed the following year, the car-sized rover continues to operate more than a decade after its original two-year mission.

*Curiosity* was launched from Cape Canaveral, Florida, on November 26, 2011, at 15:02:00 UTC and landed on Aeolis Palus inside Gale crater on Mars on August 6, 2012, 05:17:57 UTC.<sup>[3]</sup><sup>[4]</sup><sup>[5]</sup> The Bradbury Landing site was less than 2.4 km (1.5 mi) from the center of the rover's touchdown target after a 560 million km (350 million mi) journey.<sup>[6]</sup><sup>[7]</sup>

Section: *Curiosity* (rover)
The NASA/JPL Mars Science Laboratory/*Curiosity* Project Team was awarded the 2012 Robert J. Collier Trophy by the National Aeronautic Association "In recognition of the extraordinary achievements of successfully landing *Curiosity* on Mars, advancing the nation's technological and engineering capabilities, and significantly improving humanity's understanding of ancient Martian habitable environments."<sup>[14]</sup> *Curiosity*'s rover design served as the basis for NASA's 2021 *Perseverance* mission, which carries different scientific instruments.

**Perseverance**<sup>[2]</sup> is a NASA rover that has been exploring Mars since February 18, 2021,<sup>[3]</sup><sup>[4]</sup> as part of the Mars 2020 mission. Built and managed by the Jet Propulsion Laboratory, the car-sized rover was launched on July 30, 2020,<sup>[5]</sup> from Cape Canaveral aboard an Atlas V rocket and landed in Jezero Crater, a site chosen for its ancient river delta that may preserve evidence of past microbial life.

The rover's main goals are to search for signs of ancient life, study the planet's geology and climate, and collect rock and regolith samples for possible return to Earth by a future mission. *Perseverance* also tests technologies intended to support later human exploration, including an experiment that successfully produced oxygen from the thin carbon-dioxide atmosphere.<sup>[6]</sup>

Section: *Perseverance* (rover)
Powered by a radioisotope thermoelectric generator, *Perseverance* has an expected mission duration of over a decade.<sup>[11]</sup> It has provided high-resolution panoramas, drilled and cached samples for later retrieval, and identified rocks which may have been habitable for ancient microbial life in Jezero Crater. In July 2024, it discovered the Cheyava Falls rock containing "possible biosignature." As of 6 October 2026, *Perseverance* has been active on Mars for 2001 sols (2056 total days; *5 years, 230 days*) since its landing.
